Definition: from the base of G4756 and G71 or G2233; a general, i.e. (by implication or analogy) a (military) governor (prætor), the chief (præfect) of the (Levitical) temple-wardens:--captain, magistrate.
BiblicalUsage: The captain is the officer in charge, whether of the temple guard or of the city. The captain of the temple comes upon Peter and John as they speak, the magistrates of Philippi hear that Paul and Silas exceedingly trouble the city, and Jesus addresses the captains of the temple who came to take Him.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the captains show the powers that guarded the old order, and the men they arrested turned the world upside down.
